views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the already-announced August tariff schedule as leverage, but do not add a new round of hikes, entity-list expansions, or a forced corporate exit from China before List 4A even takes effect on September 1. Reopen working-level and principal talks immediately, using the August 13 split (4A Sept 1 / 4B Dec 15) and the unused October 1 25-to-30 percent process as bargaining chips rather than automatic next steps. Condition any delay or narrowing of List 4 on a verifiable return to US farm purchases plus a path back to the unfinished enforcement/IP text from the spring, not on a unilateral US rollback.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not existential. The dispute has moved from a pause at Osaka (June 29: resume talks, no new tariffs "for the time being") to a failed Shanghai round (July 30–31) and then a three-week cascade: List 4 on ~$300B (Aug 1), CNY through 7 and a currency-manipulator designation (Aug 5), a Chinese halt to US agricultural purchases (early August), and China's Aug 23 retaliation on ~$75B including soy, autos, pork and oil, met by a directed 5-point lift on List 4 (to 15%) and a threatened lift of existing 25% lists to 30%. That cascade is now biting US interests: Michigan sentiment fell from 98.4 in July to 89.8 in August, with 33% of consumers spontaneously citing the September tariff hike; the 10-year yield collapsed to 1.47% on Aug 28 versus 1.50% on the 2-year (inversion); VIX jumped to 24.59 on Aug 5 and was still 19.35 on Aug 28; the Fed had already cut funds to 2.13% in August. Farm exposure is acute — US farm sales to China fell from $19.5B (2017) to $9.1B (2018), soybean exports to China were down ~77% in the latest USDA window, and the Farm Bureau called the purchase halt a "body blow" after up to $28B in aid. List 4 is the first tranche that hits phones, laptops, toys and apparel, so consumer-price and supply-chain risk is about to widen. This sits below the +0.5 "high" anchor because industrial production is still ~102.6, the goods deficit is roughly stable (~$73.8B), Conference Board confidence remained high in late August, and China is also under strain (IP growth slowing to 4.4% y/y, yuan at 7.16). Further escalation now would likely deepen the inversion/sentiment feedback loop and invite rare-earth, unreliable-entity, or more FX offset without delivering the structural 301 outcomes that were still open in April. Unilateral concession after China's Aug 23 move would also be premature: there is no matching offer on enforcement or purchases. Negotiate-without-new-commitments is therefore the stance that matches a moderate threat: hold the announced posture, talk, and only move List 4B / the October 1 process if talks fail again.
key_factors: August cascade after Osaka pause and failed Shanghai talks (List 4, manipulator label, ag purchase halt, Aug 23 $75B Chinese retaliation plus US +5pp response)
US recession signals flashing but activity not collapsing: 10y/2y inversion, Michigan 89.8, VIX elevated, Fed already cutting; IP and Conference Board still resilient
Farm-belt and auto export exposure is the sharpest bilateral hit; List 4A (Sept 1) will shift pain onto US consumers
CNY break of 7 and 7.16 level partially offsets US tariff incidence; China IP slowing gives some remaining US leverage
No deal text on enforcement/IP since the spring; neither full rollback nor another unforced hike is justified before Sept 1

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B (cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel) delayed to Dec 15.

China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods (5–10%, split Sept 1 / Dec 15), including re-imposing tariffs on US autos. Trump directs a 5-point increase on planned List 4 and threatened hikes on existing lists.
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs for the time being.
10-year Treasury yield 1.47% on 2019-08-28, down from 2.72% in early March (~-46%).
2-year Treasury yield 1.50% on 2019-08-28; curve inverted versus the 10-year.
Michigan consumer sentiment 89.8 in August 2019, down from 98.4 in July.
CNY at 7.1628 per USD on 2019-08-28 after breaking 7 on Aug 5.
VIX 19.35 on Aug 28 after a 24.59 spike on Aug 5.
USTR (Aug 23): process to raise ~$250B from 25% to 30% effective Oct 1; List 4 10% becomes 15% on already scheduled dates.
China halted US ag purchases; Farm Bureau called it a body blow; US farm exports to China $9.1B in 2018 vs $19.5B in 2017.
Michigan: 33% of consumers spontaneously cited the proposed September China tariffs; sentiment at a multi-month low.
